audit_findings.title: Post-year-end acquisition shares are in the denominator but acquired earnings are absent from the numerator
audit_findings.magnitude: Four FY2026 acquisitions contributed $249.7 million of revenue and $15.2 million of net income through June 2026; P&S issued 437,169 shares valued at $51.459 million; OE impact unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The latest share denominator and balance-sheet bridge include post-FY2025 acquisitions, while anchor OE excludes their earnings, maintenance capex and associated financing cost.
audit_findings.evidence: On October 20, 2025, the Company acquired all of the equity interests of P&S Paving, LLC (“P&S ” ), an asphalt manufacturing and construction business headquartered in Daytona Beach, Florida, for (i) $ 98.5 million of cash, which was paid from available cash on hand and a draw from the Revolving Credit Facility, and (ii) $ 55.0 million in shares of Class A common stock.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter mismatch. Missing acquired earnings tends to understate value, while missing maintenance capex and acquisition interest tends to overstate it. The acquired businesses' reported nine-month net income equals about 24% of the $62.8 million anchor, although net income is not OE, so a consistent-perimeter rerun could materially change the valuation range.
audit_findings.action: Compute OE for the latest twelve months including VMC, P&S, GMJ and Four Star, with acquisition-date interest and maintenance capex, then rerun using the June 2026 bridge and August 2026 fully diluted shares; alternatively restore all inputs to the September 2025 perimeter.

audit_findings.title: The FY2025 perimeter ruling identifies only one of five acquisitions
audit_findings.magnitude: Five acquisitions with $1.454698 billion total purchase price contributed $673.7 million of FY2025 revenue and $30.2 million of net income; filed pro forma FY2025 net income was $139.131 million versus $101.781 million reported
audit_findings.mechanism: Staggered acquired earnings, maintenance capex and financing enter the historical OE series and log-trend anchor, while purchased growth may also be mistaken for organic growth.
audit_findings.evidence: During the 2025 fiscal year, we completed five acquisitions across four states, adding to or expanding our operations in Alabama and Tennessee and establishing our presence in Texas and Oklahoma.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter description is demonstrably incomplete. Acquired operations supplied $30.2 million of reported FY2025 net income, about 48% of the $62.8 million OE anchor as a scale comparison, and the filed full-year pro forma net-income increment was $37.350 million. Those figures are not substitutes for OE, but they demonstrate that the omitted perimeter is large enough to affect the anchor and inferred growth materially. Direction is mixed because completing the year generally adds earnings while consistent maintenance capex, interest and removal of acquisition-driven growth may reduce value.
audit_findings.action: Inventory all five acquisition dates and purchase-accounting adjustments, derive full-year pro forma OE including maintenance capex and financing, rebuild a consistent-perimeter historical series, and rerun the anchor and scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Seller consideration obligations may be omitted claims ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $44.265 million working-capital consideration payable at September 30, 2025 plus $30.0 million conditional consideration, or $74.265 million combined maximum from the supplied contracts; $1.27 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: Any surviving seller obligation is a debt-like bridge deduction because its principal is not deducted through recurring OE.
audit_findings.evidence: In addition, the Company agreed to (i) pay cash to the selling unit holders in an amount equal to the working capital remaining in Lone Star Paving at closing in the amount of $ 81.5 million, as finally determined (subject to adjustments and offsets to satisfy certain indemnification obligations and any purchase price overpayments), to be paid out in quarterly installments over four quarters following the closing and (ii) purchase from the selling unit holders for $ 30.0 million in cash an entity that owns certain real property following receipt of specified operational entitlements, which had not been received as of September 30, 2025 and expires December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The contractual claims are demonstrated, but their continued existence at June 2026 and omission from recorded liabilities are not. Even assuming both supplied amounts remained outstanding and were wholly omitted, the $74.265 million combined adjustment equals 7.6% of the $977 million base equity value and $1.27 per share, reducing base value from $16.69 to about $15.42. That cannot change the conclusion relative to the $104.68 market price.
audit_findings.action: Trace the four working-capital installments and the conditional property agreement through bank payments, acquisition settlements and June 2026 liability ledgers; deduct any surviving balance in the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Contingent acquisition consideration is another non-OE equity claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $10.734 million fair value at September 30, 2025; $20.0 million contractual maximum; approximately $0.18 and $0.34 per diluted share, respectively
audit_findings.mechanism: The outstanding earn-out is a debt-like bridge claim unless its expected settlement is explicitly included in forecast OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The stock purchase agreement includes an earn-out provision that requires the Company to pay up to $ 20.0 million to the former owners of Durwood Greene based upon the extent of the acquired business’s achievement of certain annual Adjusted EBITDA targets for a five -year period ending September 30, 2030.
audit_findings.explanation: A recognized earn-out liability is demonstrated, although its June 2026 fair value is not separately disclosed. Even the $20.0 million contractual maximum is only 2.0% of the $977 million base equity value and $0.34 per diluted share, so it cannot change the valuation conclusion relative to the $104.68 price.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the June 2026 earn-out valuation and liability roll-forward, confirm whether remeasurement or settlement was included in OE, and deduct the outstanding economic liability once rather than double counting it.

audit_findings.title: The current interest burden may not persist on the terms embedded in OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.803250 billion variable-rate debt at June 2026; $18.0 million annual pre-tax interest sensitivity per 1% rate change; $100.144 million projected FY2027 interest; $300.0 million swap expires June 30, 2027
audit_findings.mechanism: Because this is equity-level OE and debt principal is not deducted, sustainable interest expense must be charged within normalized OE and the terminal cash flows.
audit_findings.evidence: The maturity date of this swap is June 30, 2027, and the fair value of the outstanding swap contract was $7.9 million as of September 30, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The capital-structure mismatch is demonstrated: June 2026 debt exceeds the FY2025 balance, and the $300 million hedge is temporary. A one-percentage-point rate movement changes annual pre-tax interest by $18.0 million, equal to 28.7% of the $62.8 million anchor before tax. Persisting FY2025 interest terms can therefore materially overstate value, although the exact normalized after-tax burden remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Normalize OE using the June 2026 debt balances, contractual spreads, scheduled amortization, current SOFR and a post-June-2027 unhedged rate; rerun every scenario and separately disclose interest-rate sensitivity.

audit_findings.title: The entire cash balance may not be distributable excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: Maximum bridge overstatement of $94.547 million, equal to $1.62 per diluted share and 9.7% of $977 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Required operating or restricted cash must be excluded from the cash bridge rather than added as distributable value.
audit_findings.evidence: Our working capital needs are driven by the seasonality and growth of our business, with our cash requirements increasing in periods of growth.
audit_findings.explanation: The $94.547 million cash addition is demonstrated, but the amount required for operations is unresolved. The issue is bounded: even if none of the cash were excess, base value would fall from $16.69 to about $15.08 per share and bull value from $19.40 to about $17.80. That cannot change the conclusion relative to the $104.68 market price.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a seasonal minimum-cash analysis using monthly working-capital needs, remove restricted or captive-insurance amounts and near-term committed payments, and rerun the bridge with only demonstrably surplus cash.
